items.title: Eddie Locke interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York, NY, January 13, 2001
items.q: The term 'A&R guy' is used by the interviewer as a generic reference to a producer or executive involved in picking tunes for the record 'Today and Now'. The interviewee does not name a specific individual, nor does he describe a personal relationship with this unspecified role.

ctx.x: Do you suppose the A&R guy or producer whoever was picking tunes that they thought would help sell the record?

I guess it fit the way he played. I guess that’s what they were doing. Because he played that song so beautiful man. I mean that’s like one of my favorite albums that we made, was “Today and Now.” It’s beautiful music on that. And that love song from “Apache” is on there. There were some other things, “Quintessance,” that Quincy Jones tune, and I remember Monk used to always come up there. Because you know Monk loved Coleman. He loved Coleman Hawkins.
